newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Japan helps Sri Lanka upgrade health, agriculture.
newsitem.headline: Japan helps Sri Lanka upgrade health, agriculture.

text.p: The Japanese government will extend to Sri Lanka 365 million rupees ($6.4 million) of grant aid to build a school for nurses and upgrade farm equipment at a local university, a government release said on Thursday.

Japan offered 45 million rupees ($789,476) to build the national school in Sri Jayawardenapura, Kotte, a Colombo suburb, it said. Japan has already extended technical assistance to improve nursing standards, it said.
The second grant of approximately 320 million rupees ($5.6 million) will be used to upgrade educational equipment at the Faculty of Agriculture at Peradeniya University in central Sri Lanka.
Japan's ambassador in Colombo Yasuo Noguchi and Finance Secretary B.C. Perera signed the agreements in Colombo.
The grants brought the amount of aid given by Japan to Sri Lanka in 1996 to $35 million dollars, it said.
